articles.title_orig: China has changed tactics but is still thwarting India's rise, a U.S. panel says
articles.title_zh: China has changed tactics but is still thwarting India's rise, a U.S. panel says
articles.content_orig:
China is "actively working to suppress India's rise," even as the relationship between the two major Asian powers has thawed in the past year, according to a U.S. panel that sees an opening for greater outreach to India.
On Nov. 18, a U.S. China Economic and Security Review Commission report said Beijing is applying military, economic, maritime, and other forms of pressure to constrain India .
China has recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India's electronics manufacturing, slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants, and imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry, the report said.
It added that these tensions offer the U.S. an opportunity to counter growing Chinese influence by building closer ties with India across key sectors such as pharmaceutical and defense.
Ties have improved since a deadly border skirmish in 2020, but experts told CNBC that trust is still thin between Beijing and New Delhi. However, they added that the uneasy peace with China is unlikely to make India align automatically with the U.S. as an ally.
The Indian foreign and commerce ministries and the Chinese foreign ministry did not respond to emails seeking comments.
The thawing in relations between India and China came amid industrial demand, as well as the need for "a whole lot of posturing for the U.S.," said Arpit Chaturvedi, South Asia advisor at strategic advisory firm Teneo.
Over the past year, India faced tariff pressures and needed to signal to Washington that its options remain open, including that of renegotiating relations with China, he explained, but added that as the trade deal with the U.S. is "close enough now," there is no pressing need for that signaling.
Further improvement in the relationship is also limited by reports of renewed border tensions between the two sides and Beijing's scant reciprocation on easing access to technology and people movement, he said.
Last month, an Indian military official said that confrontations with Chinese soldiers were ongoing across several locations along the country's northeastern border, even as top leaders from the countries met with fanfare at the BRICS Summit in September.
Another flash point was when Beijing put export controls on tunnel boring machines last month. "Our relations with China remain good, and if there aren't any new hurdles , they can improve further," India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal reportedly said after China's move to tighten TBM exports.
On Monday, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson reportedly said Beijing is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both sides amid reports that fewer Indian businessmen got visas to attend an annual trade fair in Shanghai.
The Chinese "actively disrupt" areas where India is trying to make progress in terms of moving global supply chains, developing advanced industrial technologies such as EVs, batteries, electronic components, and pharmaceutical ingredients, Pramit Pal Chaudhuri, South Asia practice head at Eurasia Group, told CNBC.
He added China is increasingly focused on containing India economically rather than through military overtures.
India's manufacturing push still relies on Chinese inputs, from electronics components and solar materials to rare earth magnets and specialized machinery. Between April and October, India imported goods worth $96.6 billion from China , up more than 30% from a year ago, as per commerce ministry data released earlier this month.
Its major imports from China include electronic goods, machinery, chemicals, transport equipment, iron and steel, and pharmaceutical products.
While India needs inputs for its manufacturing ambitions from Beijing and China values access to Indian markets, trust between the two sides is "still thin," according to Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft, citing a large trade imbalance and overlapping interests in South Asia and the Indian Ocean as additional issues.

articles.title_zh: Mayanot Jerusalem Honors Its Partners at Rooftop Celebration
articles.content_orig:
The Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies in Jerusalem hosted a rooftop celebration honoring its supporters and bringing together alumni and friends from around the world. Full Story, Video
The Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies in Jerusalem hosted a rooftop celebration honoring its supporters and bringing together alumni and friends from around the world. Full Story, Video
The Mayanot rooftop has become a Jerusalem landmark, with its breathtaking view of the city, and stunning sunsets. Sitting at the entrance to the city, a stone’s throw from the Machane Yehuda market, and right across from Kraft Stadium, the Mayanot Institute of Jewish Studies always has its lights on and is filled with students and teachers learning at all hours of the day.
Recently, we gathered on the rooftop to honor those who helped build and create the Institute, with live music by the Solomon Brothers, and an evening dedicated to our partners and friends. We welcomed David and Eda Schottenstein , who dedicated Mayanot’s beautiful lobby; Abe and Nily Edynast , who donated the main tzedakah box; and Yitzchak Yoel and Roberta Schoen , who dedicated the library in the Beit Midrash.
Rabbi Kasriel Shemtov , Director of Mayanot, introduced Mr. Yitzchak Yoel Schoen for the dedication of the Beit Midrash library, and emphasized, “Torah is something we take with us even when we leave the walls of this yeshiva, and Mayanot endeavors to give students the tools to learn on their own so Torah learning becomes part of their life journey.”
Reb Yitzchak Yoel shared, “The real joy comes not from a plaque like this, but seeing the people use the books daily, and that’s what [Mayanot] is all about.”
David Schottenstein added that those who give to Mayanot are giving “to a place that wants to give to others. You’re building homes, you’re building Jewish homes.”
Friends and family from all 30 years of Mayanot came from around the globe to celebrate. Ken Schuckman , who studied at Mayanot in 1997, came with his sons and said, “Mayanot is probably one of the most popular places in the world! They are still my rabbis and my brothers. And now, look at this. It’s absolutely magnificent. I feel so blessed and proud to be here tonight.”
Israeli Channel 14 journalist, Yedidya Meir , said, “What’s beautiful is not the roof; it’s what happens under the roof.”  That is exactly what Mayanot is: a home for learning and growth, and for following the Rebbe’s mission of spreading light.
Eli S., a lone soldier serving in a combat unit who lives in the Mayanot dorms, said, “I came, and it was the greatest decision I’ve ever made. When I am on base, I can’t wait to get out and come home to Mayanot because it’s such an incredible environment here. This is the greatest way one who wants can contribute to lone soldiers.”
Rabbi Shlomo Gestetner , Dean of Mayanot, spoke about how every single Jew can become someone who learns Torah on a regular basis, and we have the honor and privilege of starting many journeys here at Mayanot.
We are looking forward to many more celebrations here in Jerusalem, at Mayanot, both on the rooftop and within our halls.

As part of the latest update on the Nintendo GameCube – Nintendo Classics app, a much-requested feature has finally been added for those playing via Switch Online.
Since the launch of the service in 2018, many fans have been annoyed by the borders present whenever they play a classic title. Unfortunately, there was no way to turn them off.
This didn’t just affect the GameCube app. The same issue has been present with the NES, SNES, and N64 counterparts, for example.
Thankfully, starting today, you can at least turn off the borders in GameCube games. To do so, head to “Extra Elements Display” in the settings, where you’ll find the “Border graphics” option. This can be switched on or off at any point.
Here’s a comparison between the two options:
This may not seem like a big deal for some people, but for others, it’s very significant. Some feel that they’re distracting and take away from the experience.
There are a couple of things to point out here. First, even with the border turned off, your Nintendo Switch Online icon will still be present. Additionally, so far the option is only available in Nintendo GameCube – Nintendo Classics – though it’s very likely we’ll see it roll out to the other apps at some point.
In case you missed it, Nintendo GameCube – Nintendo Classics just added Wave Race: Blue Storm today. You can find out what else is happening with Nintendo Switch Online .

articles.title_orig: Failure of Cop31 prompts calls for urgent reform of UN climate summits
articles.title_zh: Failure of Cop31 prompts calls for urgent reform of UN climate summits
articles.content_orig:
The COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, collapsed Sunday as countries failed to agree to an overarching deal after more than two weeks of contentious negotiations. The breaking point was over the very cause of climate change itself: fossil fuels.
The annual UN climate talks, which stretched deep into overtime over the weekend, hold the dubious honor of being the longest COP in history and the first major breakdown since COP15 in Copenhagen in 2009.
Experts criticized the conference as a stunning failure of leadership at a time when the climate crisis is accelerating with increasingly deadly consequences. “This has been the worst ever COP and its collapse needs to be a wake up call for the world,” said Mohamed Adow, director of the energy think tank Power Shift Africa.
How two words could derail the world’s biggest climate conference
At the final meeting intended to approve the so-called Antalya Pact on Sunday, it became clear there would not be the necessary consensus between the more than 190 countries at the talks to adopt the deal. These did not include the US, which, under President Donald Trump, has pulled out of international climate action.
Deep divisions proved impossible to bridge over key issues — most importantly, including language that the world would need to move away from fossil fuels, a phrase that did not end up in the agreement, and increasing financial support for countries already grappling with climate catastrophes. Petrostates, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, have long opposed the inclusion of any reference to fossil fuels.
The European Union, Panama, the Marshall Islands and Norway were among those that rejected it. Darragh O’Brien, Ireland’s climate minister who is helping lead negotiations for the EU, said the bloc would not endorse a deal “that does not even mention fossil fuels.”
“This COP, I believe, was hijacked by some oil states,” he later told Reuters news agency.
COP31 president Murat Kurum acknowledged support was not there to gavel through the pact. “We have done our utmost,” he said, but “it is clear that there are parties in this hall who oppose this text. We recognize that there is no consensus on this document.”
This invisible, super-polluting gas is a climate villain the world is failing to tackle
China, which is the world’s biggest climate polluter but also a clean energy superpower , called the lack of consensus a “deep disappointment.” Chinese delegation head Li Gao said the outcome shouldn’t “lead to a loss of confidence” in countries’ ability to work together to address climate change, Chinese state media Xinhua reported.
Russian delegate Sergei Kononuchenko said he cannot agree “to any formulation on fossil fuel,” according to Reuters. He added that “if supply (of oil and gas) shrinks faster than demand, the result will be not a reduction of emissions, but deficit, price shock and a switch to dirtier types of fuel and energy poverty.”
The talks come at a critical time for the planet. While attention is diverted by geopolitical turbulence — including the Iran war, which has caused the world’s largest energy supply shock — the climate crisis is accelerating.
A sobering recent UN report confirmed the world will overshoot its target of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. On current policies temperatures are expected to rise to a potentially catastrophic 2.8 degrees. The planet is currently at around 1.4 degrees of warming and the impacts have been starkly clear, from catastrophic flooding in Nepal to deadly heat in Europe.
Yet, COP31 laid bare the enormous gap between those seeking ambitious action, often the most climate-vulnerable countries, and the oil-rich nations pushing back.
In common with previous COPs, the biggest sticking point came down to two words: fossil fuels.
At COP28 in Dubai in 2023, countries agreed to an unprecedented call to “transition away from fossil fuels.” Since then, this has neither been repeated nor built upon as oil-producing nations balk at any reference to the driving force of the climate crisis.
200,000 walruses are forced ashore in Alaska as sea ice melts. Now there’s a plan to protect them
The first draft of the COP31 “cover decision” — which sets out the overarching agreement from the conference — was published Monday and called for “the immediate transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems.”
But all mentions of fossil fuels were stripped out of every subsequent draft, despite a push by more than 100 countries to keep them in. “You cannot solve a fossil fuel crisis by pretending we don’t need to phase out fossil fuels,” said Harjeet Singh, COP negotiations veteran and founding director of Satat Sampada Climate Foundation.
Britain’s lead climate negotiator Kate Hughes said the proposed agreement “moves us backwards,” describing it as “a lowest common denominator, where it should have been instead presenting bold, collective ambition on climate action.”
Meanwhile, Amnesty International’s Climate Justice policy adviser, Ann Harrison, said countries were “right to reject” what she called a “polluters’ charter designed to protect corporate profits.”
Countries and climate groups were also concerned by the agreement’s reference to increasing carbon capture technologies, which would allow for a continuation of fossil fuel production provided its carbon pollution is captured before it reaches the atmosphere.
While many scientists say the amount of carbon pollution means this technology will be needed to some extent, it remains expensive, unproven at scale and criticized as a dangerous distraction from climate policies that tackle the root cause of the crisis.
“Relying on carbon capture without phasing down fossil fuels is like trying to quit smoking without putting down the cigarettes,” said Matt Webb, associate director for global clean power diplomacy at E3G, a climate think tank.
Another huge issue of contention was finance. Poorer, climate-vulnerable countries have long called for more money to help them adapt to climate disasters they disproportionately face and yet did little to cause.
Many developing countries expressed deep disappointment that the draft agreement called for effort to at least triple adaptation finance by 2035 but included no baseline and no specific numbers.
“Rich countries refused to put money on the table to help communities prepare for and recover from climate disasters, and handed polluters a free pass instead,” Singh said. “No deal is better than a deal that locks in failure.”
COP31 president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, said the result was very disappointing but there were “a lot of good things” to come out of the talks, including more than 90 countries signing a pledge to ramp up the electrification of their economies.
“What happens now is that… will continue in our renewable transition and reconvene in Ethiopia next year and see if we can’t make forward progress,” he said.
Still, many experts expressed bitter disappointment at the world’s failure to meet the urgency of the climate crisis.
“Recognition of the dangers of overshoot should have shaken leaders into action, instead COP31 saw a shameful lack of urgency and leadership,” said Mary Robinson, the former president of Ireland and a COP veteran.

articles.title_orig: Russia’s war dead: the hidden toll of the Ukraine conflict
articles.title_zh: Russia’s war dead: the hidden toll of the Ukraine conflict
articles.content_orig:
Every 17th death registered in Russia since February 24, 2022, has been linked to the war against Ukraine, according to a leaked database from Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat) analyzed by Important Stories and more than ten other independent outlets.
The share rises to one in five in several municipalities that do not host military units. The records also show Russia's forces aging, thousands of teenagers killed, and widespread deaths from suicide and overdoses.
We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.
According to the outlets, hackers from the Silent Crow and Cyber Partisans groups obtained the civil registry archive after breaching Rosstat’s IT infrastructure in late October.
Because Russian death certificates do not include a standardized label for war fatalities, journalists identified military deaths using causes of death, locations, and occupations, noting that official Russian registrations lag behind actual battlefield losses.
Fighting near Pokrovsk in the Donetsk region and the 2024–2025 battles in Russia’s Kursk region—where North Korean troops also suffered heavy losses—accounted for some of the sharpest spikes in fatalities.
The records also reveal a steady aging of Russian forces. The median age of dead service members jumped by seven years, from 33 in 2022 to 40 in 2026, with more than 100 men over age 60 dying each month over the past three years.
At the same time, more than 7,000 teenagers aged 18 and 19 have been killed, including conscripts and young recruits who died within weeks of turning 18 after signing military contracts for money.
Foreign nationals recruited by Moscow also appear throughout the archive, alongside Ukrainian passport holders from occupied territories.
Among the documented foreign cases are a deceived Peruvian recruit who died near Pokrovsk a month after arriving in Russia, and Michael Gloss, the son of a CIA deputy director, who was killed while serving in Russia’s airborne forces.
Beyond direct combat—where explosions and shrapnel caused 92% of fatal injuries—journalists found widespread deaths linked to suicide, alcohol, and drug overdoses, primarily from methadone poisoning.
Suicide rates spiked both near the front lines and inside Russia during home leave or at rear bases, where service members took their own lives rather than return to the front.
The report comes amid continued heavy Russian losses reported by Ukrainian forces. articles.title_orig: Exclusive / Commerce adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist
articles.title_zh: Exclusive / Commerce adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist
articles.content_orig:
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.
The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.
The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.
The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.
When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.
Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.
Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.
China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.
On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee.
On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".
The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years.
The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China.
China has been blocked from buying such technology since 2022.
Although based in Singapore, Megaspeed has significant business dealings in China.
Alibaba, for instance, the major Chinese online retailer, has been reported to be one if its largest customers.
Megaspeed was a known buyer of billions of dollars of Nvidia computer chips, including through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, which has also been added to the Commerce blacklist.
Nvidia's computer chips, originally designed for use in gaming consols, in recent years have become crucial to the continued growth of the AI industry.
Without enough supply or access to computer chips that are capable of processing the huge amount of data needed to make things like AI chatbots and models run, AI companies will not be able to meet or grow demand from people using AI tools.
That has driven up the value of Nvidia on the stock market, as well as its influence in the AI industry and the White House.
Although tech stocks have in recent months been volatile and trending lower, when Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia because of his affairs, the company's stock fell by more than 30%.
Anxiety about the company's influence and ability to operate within the AI ecosystem without its famed executive appeared to take down shares of other tech companies, too.
Huang was reinstated on Monday to his position as head of Nvidia, a move that US President Donald Trump said he told the company's board to take .
The company's stock rallied on his reinstatement, as did several other tech stocks, but shares of Nvidia did not climb to where the company had been before being immersed in scandal.
In the weeks ahead, Huang and the company he now runs again are facing multiple government agency investigations.
Huang and the chief legal officer of Nvidia are set to appear next for a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

articles.title_zh: Drone attack on Colombia police base injures civilians, including infant
articles.content_orig:
A drone attack on a police base in the Colombian city of Cucuta has injured at least three civilians, including an infant, and damaged 60 homes.
Officials did not immediately say who was responsible for the attack on Monday that struck the base belonging to the Norte de Santander police.
Orlando Roa, who lives near the base, told local media that his 18-month-old grandson was among those injured and was being treated at a nearby hospital.
The attack came as far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella steps up an offensive against rebel groups and drug gangs that has resulted in the military capturing several mid-level commanders.
Armed groups have responded by attacking military bases and police stations with small drones, rockets made with gas canisters and roadside bombs. De la Espriella, who took office in August, has cancelled peace negotiations with rebel groups that were under way under his predecessor, leftist Gustavo Petro.
Cucuta, a city near Colombia’s border with Venezuela, is a major trade hub and a centre for criminal groups profiting from the drug trade and other kinds of smuggling. Rebel groups, including the National Liberation Army and the FARC-EMC, also operate in the nearby Catatumbo region.
In 2016, a peace deal between the Colombian government and the FARC led to the demobilisation of more than 14,000 fighters.
However, some border areas in Colombia have seen a surge of violence as smaller armed groups try to seize territory abandoned by the FARC, where the government has been slow to provide security and basic services.
Another police station in the Cesar region was also attacked with drones on Monday, injuring a police officer. On Saturday, one soldier was killed, and 12 others were injured during an attack with drones and rockets on a military base also in Cesar.
Both incidents remain under investigation, according to local officials.

articles.title_orig: Congress reacts with anger and skepticism about Jensen Huang reinstatement
articles.title_zh: Congress reacts with anger and skepticism about Jensen Huang reinstatement
articles.content_orig:
The stock market was thrilled with the announcement that Jensen Huang was returning as CEO of Nvidia, but lawmakers on both sides of the aisle reacted with shock — and said they still expect him to answer questions next week on Capitol Hill .
“You gotta be kidding me,” Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, told MS NOW when he learned of Huang’s reinstatement 11 days after he resigned in the wake of revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.
In its announcement, the board said it reached the decision after receiving “input from senior levels of the United States government” that his “reinstatement poses no national security risk.”
“No national security risk? Based on what?” Cornyn asked in a post on X .
President Donald Trump told CNBC he’d spoken to the board “directly and indirectly.”
“One of the things the board wanted to know, is there a national security problem?” Trump said. “And after a lot of research, we — you know, we’ve been looking at this for more than a couple of days, right? This has been a story for a few weeks. We said no, it’s not a problem.”
Lawmakers made clear they still need answers.
The Senate Banking Committee, chaired by Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., announced that Huang was scheduled to testify publicly Dec. 3.
“The national security concerns and adherence to export controls will be central to the committee’s oversight and the congressional hearing. Our markets demand transparency. Americans deserve the truth. Our committee will deliver answers,” Scott said in a statement.
A spokesperson for the House Intelligence Committee told NBC News that Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO “changes nothing” for the three House committees that are set to conduct a closed-door transcribed interview with Huang on Dec. 1.
“There are serious questions on national security implications that still need answers. Seems like the only thing that is consistent these days on this issue is our three Committee’s commitment to oversight,” the spokesperson said in a statement.
In a joint statement later Monday, the chairs of the House Select Committee on China, the Intelligence Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee said Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter “have confirmed they will appear for their transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as previously planned.”
“We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of NVIDIA products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities,” said the three Republicans, Reps. John Moolenaar of Michigan, Rick Crawford of Arkansas and Brian Mast of Florida.
The speedy reinstatement and assurances of the lack of a security risk came after the Justice and Commerce departments last week shared details about their investigation into Megaspeed , the Singapore-based company tied to Alice Huang , the suspected spy with whom Huang was allegedly involved.
Megaspeed reportedly acquired billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips and is also being investigated over concerns that it — and its subsidiaries — smuggled chips to China.
Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said in an X post that “the legal and reputational risk of hiring a CEO who may very well be convicted in the United States or other nations of violating espionage and export control laws is now born by the board of Nvidia, but the national security risk is passed along to the United States military and its citizens. The risk of extortion by a Chinese asset who’s been banned by Singapore is risk enough to not rehire Huang.”
Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., told NBC News in a phone interview “It’s not my job as a public official to tell a private company who to pick for their CEO. That’s up to the board of directors.”
But, he added, “What I want to know is whether Nvidia violated the export controls of our country with respect to advanced chips. And I want to know if the Department of Commerce did. That will be the purpose of the Banking Committee hearing.”
Sen. Jeanne Shaheen of New Hampshire, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said in a statement that the administration appears to have known about the Chinese espionage efforts targeting the Nvidia CEO for the past year and his reinstatement “without any apparent accounting or response to the risks to our national security, demands an explanation.”
Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., said the administration’s “rush to reinstate Jensen Huang underscores the need for Congress to act.”
“Trump is putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security, emphasizing that he’s learned nothing from his resounding election defeat,” Schumer said in a statement. He added that “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.”
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.”
“Congress will not be deterred from conducting a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation into business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce,” Jeffries said.
Lutnick agreed earlier this month to testify before Congress about the Huang scandal amid lawmakers’ scrutiny of China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Democrats pointed Trump’s financial ties to Nvidia, with Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the ranking member on the Oversight Committee, noting the president has a sizeable amount of Nvidia stock. “No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions,” Garcia said .
Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-Ill., cited Nvidia’s donation to Trump’s White House ballroom project as a reason to give the board’s decision extra scrutiny.
“Trump’s assurances cannot be taken at face value, especially after Nvidia’s $25 million donation to his ballroom. Huang must testify at a full public congressional hearing, with every member of the relevant committees allowed to question him,” he posted on X.
Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., questioned the Nvidia board’s decision in a post on social media.
“Jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy,” Ricketts wrote. “His own board described his behavior as lacking ‘candor.’ I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement.”
“Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen Huang from testifying before Congress,” he continued. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips. I look forward to Mr. Huang coming to the Senate in December.”
Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., called the president’s actions “Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration’s big tech and AI policy.” He told reporters it was a “good sign” that Republican senators and lawmakers have spoken out because they “realize this is a threat to national security.”
Dareh Gregorian is a politics reporter for NBC News.

NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.
“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.
“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.
The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

Nvidia’s board’s explanation for rehiring Huang should alarm everyone who cares about oversight.
Jensen Huang is CEO of Nvidia again. Eleven days after he resigned over a scandal involving an alleged affair — which China has called “ a smear ” — Nvidia’s board voted unanimously Monday to reinstate him. The scandal centered on a U.S. intelligence assertion that the woman was working for Beijing.
Wall Street cheered and the board may consider the scandal closed. It isn’t, though. As a former senior adviser on the House Oversight Committee, allow me to point out that among the things we still don’t know is who inside the Trump administration kept a suspected chip smuggler off the export blacklist — or why they did. Congress already has a list of people it intends to question about this matter, but the list of current witnesses isn’t long enough to answer all the things Congress should want to know.

In August 2025, Commerce Department investigators were reportedly months into a probe of Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company suspected of diverting Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China. That’s when, according to The New York Times and Bloomberg , Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, contacted those investigators and told them he had permission from Jeffrey Kessler, the undersecretary who oversees export controls and reports directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, to reach out. The investigators were alarmed. The Justice Department took over the case and the Commerce Department stood down. MS NOW has not confirmed this reporting.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on CNBC that the Treasury, the Pentagon, the trade representative and the State Department had all wanted Megaspeed blacklisted, “but Commerce has the pen.” The pen belongs to Lutnick. While the Commerce Department has defended its actions and claimed along with the DOJ to have “ an extremely strong track record of bringing semiconductor smugglers to justice,” Lutnick’s department has gone more than a year without adding a single company to its export blacklist. For some context, from 2018 to 2024, the Bureau of Industry and Security issued Entity List additions roughly every 35 days on average. Last week, the Commerce Department moved to close a loophole that let Chinese companies rent Nvidia’s computing power from other countries. But instead of giving anyone comfort, the move raised the question of why it took Huang’s scandal for the Commerce Department to act.
President Donald Trump defended Huang and Lutnick from the start. He says national security was never at risk, that he has no plans to replace Lutnick and that he is not sure Huang’s paramour was a spy. The New York Times reports that Trump called Huang two days before he resigned to urge him to fight for his job. On Sunday night, the president posted on social media that he hoped Nvidia’s board would rehire Huang, and by Monday morning, it had.
The board’s explanation for rehiring Huang should alarm everyone who cares about oversight. Directors say they received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and, on that basis, are confident Huang’s return poses no risk to national security. They did not say who assured them or what evidence supported that assurance. If that reported input came from the Commerce Department, then the agency accused of shielding Nvidia’s customer has now vouched for Nvidia’s chief executive. In a Monday morning interview with CNBC, Trump acknowledged that he provided input to the board .
Thus, it falls on Congress to investigate. There are many questions lawmakers should ask, including whether it was Lutnick who ignored the objections of four other agencies and decided against blacklisting Megaspeed. Is Nvidia’s lawyer’s report about getting permission from Kessler, the commerce undersecretary, true? If so, what exactly was he given permission to do, and did Lutnick know about it? Given the reports that intelligence officials briefed the president about a year ago, why was Huang never given a defensive briefing, and why did the administration keep approving Nvidia’s chip sales to China? What did Trump and Huang discuss on the phone before he resigned?
Trump tells CNBC he spoke to Nvidia board directly about Jensen Huang
What is the damage assessment? If Huang was the target of an intelligence operation, we should assume every communication he made during the relationship may have been monitored and every device he left unattended may have been opened. How much more is there? Almost none of the underlying records — the emails, the texts, the travel logs and the intelligence assessments — have reached the public yet.
Based on the current witness list, however, the investigation won’t be thorough enough to answer those questions. Lutnick has agreed to appear voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee, chaired by Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., on Dec. 10. Huang, after blowing a deadline and being threatened with a subpoena, has agreed to a closed-door , transcribed interview with three House committees on Dec. 1. Teter will follow on Dec. 2. Scott’s office says Huang will also testify in public before the Senate Banking Committee, but no date has been set. Kessler has not publicly responded to his invitation to a Dec. 3 House hearing.
Closed-door interviews are not accountability, and at this point, Huang won’t appear as a disgraced former executive but as the chief executive of the most important chip company on earth.
You’ll notice that the only fully public testimony scheduled will feature Lutnick, who gets to testify to a friendly chair a month before the gavel changes hands. Huang is scheduled to appear behind closed doors, but closed-door interviews are not accountability, and at this point, Huang won’t appear as a disgraced former executive but as the chief executive of the most important chip company on earth, with the president’s blessing and a board that has already declared itself satisfied.
When Democrats take the gavels in January, they should hold public hearings, subpoena every communication between Nvidia and the Commerce Department about Megaspeed and put Huang, Teter, Kessler and Lutnick under oath. However, because I spent years advising the House Oversight Committee, I know that in an effective investigation, you do not start with the chief executive of a company or a Cabinet secretary. You start with the junior staffers, the career export-control officers who cannot afford to pay outside counsel $1,200 an hour. You first ask the junior staffers who gave them the order to stand down. Then you work upstream.
Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Chris Coons, D-Del., have already told Lutnick, the State Department and the White House to preserve their records on Nvidia’s China sales. Everyone who touched the Megaspeed matter should assume that every email, every text and every calendar entry will become public.
Anyone who has been through a congressional investigation knows that what is public is a fraction of what exists. We have not yet seen a single email, text message or interview transcript. The Justice Department has an open criminal inquiry into Megaspeed. There is an avalanche of information that has not entered the public domain, and it’s likely that all of it will eventually. Twelve days without Jensen Huang cost Nvidia ( NVDA ) about $1.2 trillion. His first day back won most of it back in a way Wall Street hasn't seen since Cisco ( CSCO ) in 2001.

The chipmaker's board reinstated Huang as CEO Monday, and President Trump says he " convinced " them. "I don't think anybody could revive the stock like it's being revived right now," Trump said.
The stock jumped about 31%, adding about $950 billion in market value, the biggest one-day gain ever. The old record, Microsoft's ( MSFT ) $450 billion jump in July, isn't even half of it. It also tops the record one-day loss, Nvidia's own $593 billion drop on DeepSeek day in January 2025.
The surge lifted Nvidia past Microsoft and Alphabet ( GOOGL ).
Top companies change places all the time, usually by a few billion dollars. Only one other company has jumped into the top two past a rival that much bigger. On Jan. 3, 2001, a surprise Fed rate cut sent Cisco from No. 6 to No. 2 in one day, past Exxon Mobil ( XOM ), which was worth nearly 30% more.
Cisco is on the other end of the ledger, too. Its $274 billion slide from No. 1 to No. 4 in 2000 was the biggest fall from the top until this month. It never got the crown back.
Nvidia did both in three weeks. It lost nearly $2 trillion in 13 trading days, falling from No. 1 on Nov. 3 to No. 4 on Friday, including nearly $900 billion last week alone, the worst week any company has ever had.
Wall Street spent last week dumping anything tied to AI. It spent a wild Monday buying it back . Nasdaq 100 futures hit their 7% overnight limit for the first time since it was widened in 2020, and the Nasdaq 100 ( ^NDX ) closed up nearly 7%.
The rest of the chip sector came along for the ride. A Yahoo Finance basket of 62 chip stocks added about $2 trillion in market value, and about half of that was Nvidia. Memory makers SK Hynix ( SKHY ) and Micron ( MU ) rose about 20%, adding roughly $270 billion between them. Intel ( INTC ) gained 16%, while AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) lagged with single-digit gains.
Not everyone is ready to move on. Bernstein upgraded the stock on Monday but called the board's on-again, off-again response " frankly, clown-like ."
Trump isn't sweating the details. "I run the country," he said. "I don't run Nvidia, but Nvidia is a big part of it."

A tech snafu at one of the world’s busiest airports on Sunday is delaying thousands of Delta Airlines flights headed ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
An issue with Delta Airlines’ weight and balance system at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is responsible for the delay at one of the busiest airports in the country, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement posted on social media.
More than 3,550 flights traveling within, into or out of the U.S. have been delayed as of Sunday afternoon, according to Flight Aware .
The governmental agency urged travelers to check in with the airline for the latest information on their flights, and said that steps have already been taken to fix the issue.
“Delta is working to resolve issues with the airline’s weight and balance automation system,” the FAA statement said. “These delays are not related to any FAA air traffic systems.”
Delta said it is working limit congestion at its Atlanta hub.
“Delta teams are using manual workarounds to safely get flights departed while work continues to restore automation,” said Delta spokesperson Natalie Duggan. “We thank our customers for their patience and our people for their professionalism."
The issue on Sunday comes after a communications failure grounded all flights nationwide earlier this month, leading New York Gov. Kathy Hochul to call for the removal of U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.
Other recent technological malfunctions have impacted other industries, including online banking systems and Microsoft Outlook.
Delta Airlines did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Gothamist.

SHENZHEN, China — President Trump has begun an extraordinary visit to Shenzhen, where he is set to join the leaders of Russia and China — two of Washington’s principal geopolitical rivals — for an unprecedented trilateral summit Thursday.
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed Trump on the tarmac upon his arrival, reciprocating a rare honor Trump extended to him during his September visit to Washington.
All three leaders attended a dinner alongside other regional heads of government on Wednesday night, participating in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, known as APEC.
The trilateral meeting will be the first of its kind by leaders of the United States, Russia and China, three nations with the world’s largest nuclear arsenals.
But while Trump has embraced a strategy of diplomatic engagement with historic foes, the three leaders enter the meeting with starkly different agendas.
Russian President Vladimir Putin hopes to secure space and time to continue executing his war against Ukraine. Trump says he would like to discuss a nuclear arms control agreement and his war in Iran. And Xi aims to present China as a superpower on the international stage, capable of forging world peace.
Meeting with Putin before Trump arrived, Xi said that China’s relationship with Russia had remained as steadfast “as a rock through wind and rain.”
The two sides, he said, would pursue a “multipolar world” — a vision for a global balance of power that would see American influence weakened across Europe and Asia.
A new rule tightening loopholes in U.S. export controls sends a dual message to Beijing ahead of Thursday’s summit.
Trump, for his part, has hedged on his expectations of the summit, signaling resolve against China ahead of his arrival here.
On Monday, the Trump administration tightened export controls on semiconductor chips essential to artificial intelligence development, closing loopholes aimed at curbing Chinese efforts to circumvent restrictions — a move that Trump acknowledged might be an “insult” to Xi before the meeting.
Chinese officials said Wednesday afternoon that Beijing reserved the right to retaliate.
“In essence, the United States is simultaneously trying to find limited avenues of cooperation with China while trying to clamp down on their access to critical parts of the AI supply chain, which doesn’t set up the conditions for productive dialogue,” said Aalok Mehta, director of the Wadhwani AI Center at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
Trump also met in Manila on Tuesday with fellow members of the Quad — India, Japan and Australia — in a show of resolve toward Beijing.
“Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Trump said in the Philippines.
“We continue to protect peace through strength,” he added.

articles.title_orig: States sue Musk companies over flood of sexualized images made with AI chatbot Grok
articles.title_zh: States sue Musk companies over flood of sexualized images made with AI chatbot Grok
articles.content_orig:
Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the company over issues with its Grok AI image generator.
Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled users to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation , the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others.
In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X users from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material.
The complaints also allege that SpaceX has falsely represented its AI apps and social network (Grok and X) as generally safe, which the states see as a violation of Virginia's Consumer Protection Act or Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The matter is particularly concerning because X allows minors 13 and older to access its content.
Rayfield and Jones both noted in their complaints that harms caused by non-consensual, sexualized images go beyond the victims depicted in the images.
"This content can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content," Jones wrote. Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes important norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation."
In a statement emailed to CNBC by a spokesperson for SpaceXSI, and posted on the company's @Safety account on X, the company said, "When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement. Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors."
At an NYC Council hearing in October , a SpaceX AI policy leader, Gabriela Castillo Madrid, said the company had appropriate "safeguards" and "strict controls" in place around its AI products.
SpaceX was already facing multiple Grok- and X-related lawsuits, and government probes around the world, including by authorities in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and the state of California.
In private-sector lawsuits filed against SpaceX in the U.S. concerning Grok and AI-generated, explicit images, litigation is still in early stages and is tracked by The Center for Internet Technology Addiction.
When the city of Baltimore sued xAI, now owned and operated by SpaceX, the company argued that under Section 230, they were not liable for unwanted images. Section 230 is a federal law that largely shields online platforms from liability for users' content.
SpaceX also sued a user in a federal court in the Northern District of Texas for breach of contract after he allegedly used Grok to create and distribute deepfake explicit images, including depictions of minors. Lawyers for Musk's company argued that Grok should be seen as "a neutral tool, subject to user control," and that any image generation "is the result of the user's prompts and directions."
The new state suits add to legal pressure on SpaceX. Both Virginia and Oregon are seeking injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs, while Virginia is also seeking restitution for consumers from Musk's company.
Oregon submitted its complaint to the Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening, and Virginia submitted its complaint to the City of Richmond Circuit Court Monday morning . As of early Monday, the suits were pending the courts' acceptance.
State attorneys general have recently succeeded in compelling U.S. social media companies to change their products and pay for alleged past harms.
In August, for example, Meta settled a major federal case centered on allegations that the social media giant misrepresented the level of child mental health problems caused by its apps, Facebook and Instagram . Without admitting to wrongdoing, Meta agreed to pay states around $17 billion over a 10-year period and to make app changes that experts believe will help keep children safer online.

articles.title_zh: Xi pressed Trump on Taiwan at meeting in China, urged U.S. to halt arms sale
articles.content_orig:
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney shakes hands with China's President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit on Nov. 19, 2026.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is placing particular focus on renewing relations with China as he aims to deepen international trade ties and diversify from U.S. reliance amid a three-month-long trade war with the U.S.
When asked what cards Canada holds in its ongoing talks with Washington, Carney, who recently announced a new partnership with the E.U. , pointed to the country's budding relationships elsewhere.
“Our cards are that everyone else in the world wants to deal with us,” he said Wednesday during a remote interview with the New York Times from Shenzhen, China, where he was among the world leaders attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit . "If the U.S. doesn't want to do the deal, we're busy.” His remarks came in the wake of President Donald Trump's claim that the U.S. holds “all the cards” after trade talks collapsed in August, leading to both sides enforcing heavy retaliatory tariffs .
Carney and Trump had a meeting on the sidelines of APEC, but aside from a commitment to “continue” negotiations and stay in close contact, no progress was made. However, Carney painted his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in a much more positive light. Ahead of the summit, Carney and Xi announced a Canada-China trade pact , which provided additional tariff relief on Canadian food and agricultural exports into China, and in return saw Canada agree to extend tariff exemptions for certain Chinese steel and aluminum products by two years.
Carney, who is promoting a “Canada Strong” platform as he aims to build economic resilience at home, touted the expansion of the trade arrangement with China as something that will deliver “greater certainty and prosperity for all Canadians.” He also praised the negotiation process with China, saying: “They’re very professional. They move forward in a very linear fashion.”
In an eight-day tour that took him from a European summit in Ireland to the Philippines, Cambodia, and finally China for the APEC gathering, Carney forged ahead with his plan to diversify Canada's economy away from its dependence on the U.S., which by far remains the country's largest trading partner .
Experts say Canada's progress in deepening its economic relationships with China could challenge Trump's insistence that Washington holds the upper hand in trade negotiations.
“Part of the Trump Administration’s [belief] is that everybody needs the U.S. more than anything else, and therefore the U.S. has maximum leverage,” says Jennifer Hillman, co-director of the Institute of International Economic Law at Georgetown University. “What this is clearly saying is that Canada can afford to be less willing to give the U.S. whatever it asks for [in negotiations], because they have other options.”
China has the world's second-largest economy , behind only the U.S., giving it the potential to become a much larger market for Canadian goods than some of the other countries Carney has sought to deepen relations with.
“China represents a very big market and the potential of a really big trading partner,” says Lori Turnbull, a professor in the Faculty of Management at Dalhousie University, noting it could be a leverage point in U.S. negotiations. “Doing a deal with a country like China is something that [the U.S.] will care about because of the size of China's economy and its competitive relationship with the U.S.”
Carney's latest push to strengthen trade ties with Beijing forms part of a months-long effort to renew Canada-China relations. In January, he met with Xi to forge what he called a “ new strategic partnership ,” agreeing to allow in up to 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles at a tariff of 6.1%, rather than the previous 100% levy. China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, including canola seeds, a major Canadian export.
The move drew criticism from Trump, who said that “China will eat Canada alive, completely devour it, including the destruction of their businesses, social fabric, and general way of life.”
While Canada's closer relationship with China could strengthen its hand in negotiations, experts also warn that it could backfire.
Turnbull points to the latest agreement to extend tariff exemptions on Chinese steel and aluminum as a potential source of tension with Washington. “Things like reducing tariffs on select steel and aluminum products coming from China is something that might make the U.S. and not just Donald Trump, but also [U.S. Trade Representative] Jamieson Greer angry,” she suggests.
Steel, aluminum, and auto tariffs were among the major points of contention when U.S.-Canada trade negotiations broke down in August, with both sides accusing each other of walking back commitments.
Carney, however, has played down concerns that Canada's growing trade relationship with China is a major issue for Trump.
“In my conversation with the President, he’s tried to understand where we are with China, where we’re going with China,” said Carney during a news conference in Shenzhen. “I shouldn’t speak for him, but in his hierarchy of issues, it’s not the top issue at all.”
Meanwhile, some Canadian officials have voiced concerns on expanding trade with China.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned Carney on Monday against opening the door for more Chinese-made EV vehicles in Canada, arguing the “government’s focus needs to be on protecting Canadian auto workers, not undermining them by importing even more state-subsidized cheap Chinese cars.”
Michael Chong, a lawmaker from Canada’s Conservative Party, during a press conference on Wednesday supported maintaining a dialogue with Beijing, but described Carney’s budding strategic partnership with China as a “risky gambit,” citing potential “national security” concerns.
In 2025, Ottawa identified China as one of the main perpetrators of foreign interference and espionage against Canada alongside other countries such as Russia and Iran. The Canadian government’s own analysis of Canada-China relations also points out that there are "associated risks” in broader trade cooperation in key areas, such as “prevalent and persistent intellectual property theft, and the risk of diversion of sensitive goods and technologies intended for civilian use for military purposes and applications.”
Carney said ahead of his Asia trip that he would raise concerns about foreign interference in his meeting with Xi. "The advantage of these meetings is you can raise issues directly and frankly,” he told reporters in Montreal on Nov. 10. Carney added that he would stress the importance Canada places on "the non-interference in our affairs by China and other countries.”
In a press briefing during the APEC summit, Carney emphasized that Canada's trade with China is largely focused on commodities, rather than sensitive technologies such as advanced semiconductors.
“We are exporting canola, we are exporting pork. We are exporting halibut,” Carney said , also citing liquefied natural gas and oil. “These are important industries. These are not cutting-edge semi-conductors.”
Experts point out that Canada could pursue deeper cooperation with other international partners in sectors where a closer relationship with China would be more difficult, including defense and advanced technology.
“[Canada] is not going to partner with China on defense, security, AI, and digital technology, things like that would be very difficult. [Carney] would have an impossible time trying to convince Canadians that's what we should be doing,” says Turnbull. “For those things, [Canada] would be putting [its] arms around the European Union.”

articles.title_zh: New York judge urged Kalshi to compromise on limiting bets by anyone under 21
articles.content_orig:
The move came after the New York AG sought a TRO against the prediction market.
The Trump administration tried unsuccessfully to step in after an attorney for the prediction market Kalshi warned Friday that the platform could be crippled if a judge grants a temporary restraining order being sought by New York state's attorney general.
New York Attorney General Letitia James requested the restraining order after U.S. District Judge Vernon Broderick on Friday denied Kalshi's attempt to move James' lawsuit against the platform from New York state court into federal court, ruling that prediction markets do not necessarily fall outside state jurisdiction.
After James asked New York Judge Melissa Crane to issue the restraining order to stop Kalshi from offering sports contracts without a license from the New York State Gaming Commission, Kalshi attorney Sean Murphy told Crane that "The TRO would likely force the liquidation of all open positions, disrupting markets far beyond this State."
Judge Crane set a hearing on the matter for Monday.
In an emergency telephone hearing Friday, the Trump administration urged another federal judge, Lorna Schofield, to prevent Crane from ruling on the TRO request.
"The temporary restraining order New York seeks would completely shut down Kalshi's operations nationwide," said Andrew Weisberg, an attorney for Kalshi's regulator, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. "There is no greater irreparable harm than one of our regulated markets being completely disrupted."
An attorney for the New York attorney general's office, Kate Rhodes Janofsky, countered that there is no basis for the federal judge to intervene when there is a hearing in state court scheduled for Monday.
"They have to put in evidence of irreparable harm. They have not done so. There has been no evidence of market disruption," Janofsky said.
Judge Schofield agreed and declined to get involved. "The requested application is denied," she said.
James sued Kalshi in July , claiming that the platform violates New York state laws prohibiting wagering on games involving New York college teams and all sports betting for those under 21.
The lawsuit does not seek to shut Kalshi down -- but, if successful, it could force the prediction market to change the way it operates.

If you’ve been waiting for an excuse to upgrade your home audio while supporting a good cause, here’s your chance. Apple is planning to revive it s Product Red charity partnership with new versions of the HomePod Mini 2 and AirPods Max 2, according to a Bloomberg report . The $149 HomePod Mini 2 came out in early November and will now be offered with a red mesh cover as part of this collaboration. The AirPods Max 2 will come in silver, instead of red, but will feature a red digital crown.
While Apple has released red phone cases in the meantime, the last hardware collaboration came in 2018, when the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus were released in Product Red colors. Red cases were also released.
A representative for Apple didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
Read more: Best Smart Speakers of 2026
The release would coincide with the 20th anniversary of the first Product Red collaboration, the iPod Nano Red Special Editio n. For that event, Apple contributed $10 from the sale of each device to the Global Fund to help fight HIV/AIDS in Africa. Product Red was founded in 2006 by politician Bobby Shriver and Bono of the band U2, and the iPod Nano Red special edition included music from U2.
Apple has yet to announce pricing and availability for the two devices. But according to the report, the product could be available Dec. 1, which is designated as World AIDS Day.

articles.title_orig: Amazon’s China-made adult bed rails recalled after 89-year-old woman dies of suffocation
articles.title_zh: Amazon’s China-made adult bed rails recalled after 89-year-old woman dies of suffocation
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of adult bed rails from China that were sold in the US have been recalled after an 89-year-old woman died of suffocation when she was trapped between the product and her mattress.
About 2,114 adult bed rails sold on Amazon by Guangzhou Yupin Technology Co. – a Chinese company doing business as Xentrawave – are included in the recall, according to the US Consumer Product Safety Commission.
All batches of Xentrawave’s model XT016 and batch number 20251212 of model XT026 are included in the recall for failing to meet mandatory safety requirements, because customers can be pinned between the rail and the side of the mattress – posing a risk of death by asphyxiation.
The XT106 model adult bed rail also doesn’t meet structural stability requirements and its push pins and push pin holes are incorrectly sized, posing a risk of laceration, the agency said.
The CPSC said it has received one report of a death related to the Xentrawave recall, involving the 89-year-old woman who died from asphyxiation.
Customers can find the model numbers XT016 or XT026 on the front of the product’s outer packaging and the first page of the instruction manual.
For the XT026 model, consumers can locate the batch number on the product label attached to the back of the bed rail’s gray fabric pouch and in the instruction manual.
Consumers should immediately stop use of the recalled bed rails and contact Xentrawave for a full refund.
Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.
They will be asked to cut the foam padding on the bed rail handles, disassemble the product and email a photo of the destroyed bed rail to xentrawavedirect@163.com or submit it online at https://xentrawahelp.com/xentrawave-bed-rail-safety-recall/ .
The recalled XT016 bed rails were sold on Amazon from May 2025 through March 2026 and the XT026 model was sold from March 2026 through August 2026. The bed rails cost between $37 and $40.
The bed rails were manufactured by China-based Guangzhou Nanyu Medical Technology Co.

Update [ Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 2:50pm ]: Well, the patch notes are out! Rockstar Games mentions seven official fixes for the update, and none of them are specifically to do with the Xbox Series S or other things like how bright the game is.
Nevertheless, there's always a chance they've made some extra tweaks under the hood.
Here are the official seven fixes in GTA 6's first post-launch update (November 23):
Original Story: GTA 6 only officially launched late last week, but Rockstar Games has already pushed out a new update (01.002.002) for the game across Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S (along with PS5), rolling out as of a few hours ago.
You're looking at a download size of around 1.6GB for update 1.0.2 on Xbox Series X and S.
In terms of what's included, Rockstar has yet to issue any official patch notes, and we'll have to wait and see whether anything is distributed. We'll obviously update this article with the patch notes if they're made available to us.
Players are trying to make their own discoveries in the meantime, with suggestions that the game may run smoother on Xbox Series S now, that saving your game returns you to the exact same spot instead of your safehouse (although this seemed to be happening for us already), and that the first-person glitch is still working as things stand.
All of these could be akin to placebo effects though, so take them with a pinch of salt:
As you can see from one of the impressions above, there's a suggestion that the game seems brighter now, which perhaps could have something to do with the borked HDR calibration tool that we discussed the other day .
That said, who knows whether these are areas that have actually been targeted for the update, or whether they're just happy coincidences that some players are experiencing. In any case, we'll keep an eye out for any official confirmations.
